title: Localizations of Nagata rings are Nagata
statement: Let $A$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and let $T\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative subset ($1\in T$, $st\in T$ for $s,t\in T$), with localization $T^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $T^{-1}A$ is a Nagata ring: it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T^{-1}A$ the domain $(T^{-1}A)/\mathfrak q$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. In particular each local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and each principal localization $A_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is Nagata.

proof.text: For an arbitrary submonoid U, use Noetherianity of A and IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing to obtain Noetherianity of Localization U.

For a prime q of Localization U, contract to p = q.under A. IsLocalization.isPrime_iff_isPrime_disjoint gives primality and disjointness, so the image S of U in A/p avoids zero. IsLocalization.map_under and IsLocalization.of_surjective make (Localization U)/q an S-localization of A/p; IsLocalization.algEquiv identifies it with Localization S.

Apply localization_isN1_isN2 to A/p, FractionRing(A/p), S and the zero-avoidance proof, and apply its N-2 implication to hA.2 p. The resulting fraction-field algebra structure is determined by the explicit fraction formula in that theorem.

Give (Localization U)/q its Localization S-algebra structure via the canonical ring equivalence. This map is injective and finite, since it is surjective. Localization S is Noetherian, since A/p is Noetherian. Apply isN2_of_finite_domain_extension along this equivalence, using the fraction fields FractionRing(A/p) and FractionRing((Localization U)/q); this transports the N-2 condition. Assemble the two Nagata clauses.
Specialize the argument to U = T, U = p.primeCompl and U = Submonoid.powers f, using the definitions of AtPrime and Away.
